sources.search_query: official Philippines evisa portal Department of Foreign Affairs
sources.relevant_excerpt: The eVisaPH system is an "Electronic Visa Online" application platform. The system was "developed by" the Department of Foreign Affairs (DFA), Department of Information and Communications Technology (DICT), Department of Tourism (DOT), National Intelligence Coordination Agency (NICA), Bureau of Immigration (BI), and Department of Justice (DOJ). The process involves registering, filling forms, uploading documents, making payment, potentially submitting original documents, and receiving the eVisa "via email and registered e-Visa account."

sources.search_query: official Philippines evisa portal Department of Foreign Affairs
sources.relevant_excerpt: "Nationals of other countries not indicated/included in the above-mentioned Executive order No. 408 are considered VISA-REQUIRED NATIONALS." These individuals must meet a "more stringent set of documentary and other requirements per Philippine Codified Visa Rules and Regulations." Applicants can pursue Philippine visa applications at embassies and consulates abroad. The portal describes visa categories 9(a-1) through 9(a-8).

sources.search_query: official Philippines evisa portal Department of Foreign Affairs
sources.relevant_excerpt: 9(a-2) Tourism/Leisure Visitors: "Foreign nationals visiting the Philippines temporarily for pleasure or touristic, leisure, religious, recreation, or amusement purposes". Minimum requirements: flight reservations for entry and exit; financial capacity documentation (bank statements, employment certificates, or sponsor guarantees); proof of ties to home country; hotel accommodation or lodging proof; parental permission for minors traveling alone. "issued Philippine e-Visas are not valid for conversion to other types of Philippine visas, and are not valid for extension of the authorized period of stay."

sources.search_query: official Philippines evisa portal Department of Foreign Affairs
sources.relevant_excerpt: "Foreign nationals can apply for a Philippine e-Visa if they are travelling to the country for business, pleasure, medical treatment, training, attendance in conferences, meetings and workshops/seminars, and other purposes." "The processing time of e-Visas will be 7-12 working days for single entry and 15-21 working days for multiple entries." The eligible Country of Citizenship list and the fee amount load dynamically and were not retrievable from the static page.

sources.search_query: site:immigration.gov.ph temporary visitor visa 9a visa waiver tourist
sources.relevant_excerpt: Bureau of Immigration Philippines. The site lists a "Temporary Visitor Visa (9A)" under Non-Immigrant Visa options. There is a "Visa Waiver" program with a dedicated e-Service available at their online portal, and a "Tourist Visa Extension" service accessible through their e-Services platform. The website directs travelers to the eTravel System, described as the "Philippine One-Stop Electronic Travel Declaration System". The BI acts as "the primary enforcement arm of the Department of Justice".

sources.search_query: site:immigration.gov.ph temporary visitor visa 9a visa waiver tourist
sources.relevant_excerpt: Temporary Visitor (9A) Visa Waiver. Eligibility: "Non-visa required tourists admitted initially for thirty (30) days and is requesting for an initial extension of twenty-nine (29) days". Fees (Philippine Peso) for the initial 30+29 day authorization: Visa Waiver P500, Application Fee P1,000, Certification Fee P500, Legal Research Fee P30, Express Fee P1,000, Total P3,030. Overstay penalty P500 per month. Requirements include the CGAF "from either at the Public Information and Assistance Unit (PIAU) at BI G/F Main Office or from the official BI Website", passport, and documentary checklist items. Special passport holders (Macau-Portuguese, Hong Kong-British, and Hong Kong SAR passports) have varying initial admissions of 7 or 14 days.

sources.search_query: site:immigration.gov.ph temporary visitor visa 9a visa waiver tourist
sources.relevant_excerpt: "Foreign nationals under E.O. 408, as amended, admissible for thirty (30) days initial stay." Extensions: "non-visa required national may extend their stay up to thirty six (36) months while visa required national may extend their stay up to twenty four (24) months." Extensions available for "one (1) month, two (2) months or six (6) months" with application "at least one week prior to the expiration of your valid stay." Visa Upon Arrival options mentioned: "Visa Upon Arrival VA thirty (30) days", group tours under Memorandum Order, Pro-Investment Visa under Memorandum Circular.

sources.search_query: Philippine Embassy Washington DC tourist visa 9a fees visa-free entry official site
sources.relevant_excerpt: 9(A) Temporary Visitor's Visa fees: visa-free nationals "USD 30", Chinese nationals "USD 25", non-visa-free nationals "USD 40"; all fees "non-refundable", paid by money order to "Embassy of the Philippines". Passport must be "valid for at least six months upon entry". "Roundtrip or onward ticket out of the Philippines with a departure date within 59 days (for visa-free nationals) or 30 days (for non-visa-free nationals) of arrival." "Certain international travelers may be eligible to travel to the Philippines without a visa if they meet the requirements for visa-free travel."

sources.search_query: Philippine Embassy Washington DC tourist visa 9a fees visa-free entry official site
sources.relevant_excerpt: Temporary Visitor Visa (9A). Visa-free country nationals: "Single Entry $30" valid three months, "Multiple Entry $60" valid six months, "Multiple Entry $90" valid one year. Non visa-free country nationals: "Single Entry $40", "Multiple Entry $80" (six months), "Multiple Entry $120" (one year). Chinese nationals: "Single Entry $25", "Multiple Entry $50" (six months), "Multiple Entry $100" (one year). Transit Visa 9(B): "$20".

sources.search_query: Bureau of Immigration Philippines Indian nationals visa-free entry 14 days announcement 2025
sources.relevant_excerpt: Effective 8 June 2025, Indian nationals may enter for a "non-extendible and non-convertible period of 14 days for tourism purposes" upon presenting a passport valid for at least six months beyond the contemplated stay, confirmed hotel booking, proof of financial capacity, and return or onward ticket. Indian nationals holding valid American, Japanese, Australian, Canadian, Schengen, Singapore, or UK (AJACSSUK) visas or residence permits may enter without a visa for a "non-extendible period of 30 days for tourism". Both options are "not convertible to a visa-based stay or other admission status categories"; applicants must have no derogatory immigration records.
